products.technicalOverview:
5-Amino-1MQ is a permanently charged quinolinium cation supplied as its chloride salt. It is a substrate-site inhibitor of nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT), the cytosolic enzyme that methylates nicotinamide to 1-methylnicotinamide using S-adenosylmethionine as the methyl donor. Because that reaction consumes nicotinamide, NNMT activity sits directly upstream of the salvage route into NAD+; inhibiting it is the reason the compound appears in NAD+ and cellular-energy literature rather than any direct action on NAD+ itself.

A note on identity: the CAS number 42464-96-0 is quoted by many suppliers for the chloride, but that registry number resolves to the iodide salt (C10H11N2·I, MW 286.11) in Sigma-Aldrich's catalogue and in ChemicalBook's own property block. Because the two assignments conflict, no CAS is asserted here for the chloride. The molecular formula and weight above describe the chloride salt as supplied.

Evidence is preclinical. The most-cited work (Neelakantan et al., 2018) reported that membrane-permeable small-molecule NNMT inhibitors of this class reduced adiposity in diet-induced obese mice; there are no controlled human outcome data. Interpret any metabolic claim accordingly.
products.researchApplications: Used as a tool compound for NNMT enzyme-inhibition assays, methylation-flux and 1-methylnicotinamide quantification work, and adipocyte differentiation and lipid-accumulation models. Also used in NAD+ salvage-pathway studies where the goal is to raise nicotinamide availability by blocking its methylation rather than by supplementing a precursor. Common readouts are LC-MS/MS measurement of 1-methylnicotinamide and SAM/SAH ratios, cellular NAD+ pools, and adipocyte lipid staining.

Keep any desiccant in the bottle and re-close tightly after each opening — capsule shells take up atmospheric moisture and will soften or stick together in humid conditions. Do not refrigerate; condensation on return to room temperature is the usual cause of capsule degradation. Keep the container labelled as research material and out of reach of children and animals.

products.technicalOverview:
5-Amino-1MQ is a small, permanently charged quinolinium cation carrying an amino substituent at the 5-position and a methyl group on the ring nitrogen. Despite the fixed positive charge it is reported to be membrane-permeable, which is the property that distinguishes it from earlier bisubstrate NNMT inhibitors and makes cell-based and whole-animal work practical.

Its described target is nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT), a cytosolic enzyme that transfers a methyl group from S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) to nicotinamide, producing 1-methylnicotinamide and S-adenosylhomocysteine. Because nicotinamide is a salvage-pathway precursor of NAD+, NNMT activity sits at a junction between methyl-group economy and NAD+ availability; inhibiting the enzyme is the mechanistic rationale behind investigating this compound in adipocyte metabolism and NAD+-related pathway models.

Identity note: this material is most often supplied as a salt rather than the free cation, and the salt form is not stated on the product record. Published and vendor sources disagree on which registry number belongs to which salt — one widely circulated page pairs a chloride name with an iodide molecular formula — so no CAS number is asserted here. Confirm the counter-ion, salt stoichiometry and assigned registry number against the lot-specific certificate of analysis before using this material in any quantitative work, since salt form changes the molar mass and therefore every concentration calculated by weight.

The evidence base is preclinical. Reported effects come from cell culture and rodent studies; no human clinical trial data are cited here.
products.researchApplications: Used in vitro and in rodent models as a chemical probe of NNMT function. Reported preclinical applications include: interrogation of adipocyte lipid handling and energy expenditure in diet-induced obesity models; study of the SAM/methylation and NAD+ salvage axis and how NNMT inhibition redistributes flux between them; and investigation of muscle stem cell proliferation, fusion and regenerative capacity in aged skeletal muscle. Appropriate experimental controls include an NNMT-null or knockdown comparator and direct measurement of 1-methylnicotinamide, since a fall in that metabolite is the most direct readout of on-target engagement.

Store the dry solid desiccated at -20 °C, protected from light and moisture; the compound is reported to be soluble in DMSO and in aqueous buffer. Prepare concentrated stocks in anhydrous DMSO, aliquot to avoid repeated freeze-thaw cycles, and store aliquots at -20 °C or below. Allow vials to equilibrate to room temperature before opening to prevent condensation onto hygroscopic solid. Weigh in a fume hood and handle with gloves and eye protection. Calculate molarity from the salt form stated on the certificate of analysis, not from the free-cation mass.

products.technicalOverview:
Akkermansia muciniphila is an oval, non-motile, strictly anaerobic bacterium first described by Derrien and colleagues in 2004. It was isolated from human faeces and characterised by its unusual metabolic niche: it uses host-secreted intestinal mucin as its sole source of carbon and nitrogen, and it colonises the mucus layer overlying the epithelium rather than the lumen. It is a normal member of the adult human gut community, typically making up a low single-digit percentage of total faecal bacteria.

Interest in the organism comes from repeated observations that its relative abundance is lower in obesity, type 2 diabetes and inflammatory bowel conditions, and from rodent work linking colonisation to mucus-layer thickness and barrier function. A proof-of-concept human study (Depommier et al., Nature Medicine 2019) administered live and pasteurised A. muciniphila to overweight and obese volunteers over three months; it was designed to test feasibility and safety rather than to demonstrate efficacy, and its metabolic findings were exploratory.

The evidence base has since become more nuanced rather than more certain. A 2025 Cell Metabolism trial reported that the response to supplementation depended on the participant's own baseline Akkermansia level, which is a reminder that this is a colonisation-dependent intervention, not a dose-response drug. Potency here is expressed in AFU (active fluorescent units), a flow-cytometry count of intact cells, which is not interchangeable with the CFU counts used for culturable probiotics.
products.researchApplications: Used in gut-microbiome composition and intervention studies, intestinal barrier and mucus-layer integrity models, and host–microbe signalling work involving the Amuc_1100 outer-membrane protein and TLR2. Typical readouts are 16S rRNA or shotgun metagenomic quantification of relative abundance, faecal and mucosal colonisation, short-chain fatty acid profiles, tight-junction protein expression, and circulating markers of endotoxaemia.
products.storageHandling: Refrigerate at 2–8 °C (36–46 °F) in the sealed original bottle; viability and the stated AFU count are time- and temperature-dependent, and warm or humid storage will degrade the count well before the printed date. Keep away from light and moisture, keep the desiccant in the bottle, and re-close tightly. Do not freeze. Because this is a live/pasteurised bacterial preparation rather than a chemical, do not repackage into unlabelled containers, and handle with the same care as any other biological material in the laboratory.

products.technicalOverview:
AOD-9604 is a synthetic peptide corresponding to the C-terminal fragment of human growth hormone (residues 177–191) with an additional tyrosine residue at the N-terminus. It also circulates under the name Tyr-hGH fragment 176-191, and both stylings appear in supplier listings — they describe the same molecule.

The peptide was designed to reproduce the lipolytic region of growth hormone without the diabetogenic effects of the full protein. That framing is best read as design intent rather than a demonstrated result: the primary literature characterising the compound is analytical, and its functional claims are reported rather than established.

In vitro incubation in serum and urine has identified six potential metabolites. Of these, the sequence CRSVEGSCG proved significantly more stable than the parent compound itself — a useful inversion for method development, where the parent is not necessarily the best analyte to target.

Note that the unmodified hGH fragment 176-191 is a different peptide with its own CAS number, lacking the N-terminal tyrosine. The two are not interchangeable and should not be treated as the same material.

products.technicalOverview:
ATX-304 is a synthetic small molecule, not a peptide. Product copy in this category sometimes describes it as a peptide analogue acting on angiogenic signalling; that is incorrect. It is an orally bioavailable benzothiazole originally developed as O304 at Umeå University and Betagenon AB, and it is classed as a first-in-class direct pan-activator of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK).

Mechanistically it does not mimic AMP at the γ-subunit nucleotide sites. It raises AMPK activity by suppressing dephosphorylation of the activation-loop residue Thr172, so phosphorylated AMPK persists longer; a mitochondrial uncoupling contribution has also been reported. Because it activates all AMPK heterotrimer combinations rather than one isoform, downstream effects span skeletal muscle glucose uptake, hepatic lipid handling and microvascular perfusion.

The evidence is early-stage. Steneberg et al. (JCI Insight, 2018) reported improved glucose homeostasis and microvascular perfusion in diet-induced obese mice and, in a small phase IIa proof-of-concept cohort of type 2 diabetes patients already on metformin, reductions in fasting plasma glucose and HOMA-IR. A later study in aged mice reported improvements in metabolic and cardiac function and exercise capacity. There are no completed large controlled efficacy trials, and no approved indication.
products.researchApplications: Used as a direct AMPK-activating tool compound in skeletal muscle and hepatocyte energy-metabolism models, mitochondrial bioenergetics work, and microvascular perfusion studies. Typical readouts are phospho-AMPK (Thr172) and phospho-ACC immunoblotting, cellular oxygen consumption and extracellular acidification rates, glucose uptake in myotubes, and in vivo glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity testing. Also used as a comparator against indirect activators such as metformin and AICAR.

This is a four-component blend, so no single CAS number, formula or molecular weight describes it. Each component is summarised below.

ATX-304 (also called O-304 or OS-01) is a synthetic benzothiazole small molecule, CAS 1261289-04-6, formula C16H11Cl2N3O2S. It is a direct pan-activator of AMP-activated protein kinase that works by suppressing dephosphorylation of AMPK at Thr172. Preclinical work reported improved glucose homeostasis and microvascular perfusion in obese mice, with a small phase IIa signal in type 2 diabetes patients on metformin. Note that it is a small molecule, not a peptide analogue.

Myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol are naturally occurring cyclitol stereoisomers and the precursors of the inositol phosphoglycan second messengers that sit downstream of the insulin receptor. They are studied together, usually at a fixed ratio, in insulin-signalling and ovarian-function research. They are nutrient-derived compounds rather than novel chemical entities.

products.compoundClass: Purine nucleoside analogue; AMP mimetic and indirect AMPK activator
products.sequence: Not applicable — small-molecule compound, not a peptide (no amino acid sequence)
products.technicalOverview:
AICAR, also called acadesine or AICA riboside, is a nucleoside analogue of the purine biosynthesis intermediate 5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide. Note the nomenclature carefully: the material supplied here is the riboside (nucleoside), not the ribotide monophosphate that shares the AICAR acronym in purine-pathway textbooks. The riboside is the cell-permeable form used experimentally.

Once inside the cell, adenosine kinase phosphorylates it to ZMP, which mimics AMP at the γ-subunit nucleotide-binding sites of AMP-activated protein kinase. That makes AICAR an indirect AMPK activator: it does not bind the kinase's catalytic site, it raises the apparent AMP:ATP signal. Because ZMP is a promiscuous AMP mimic it also acts on other AMP-sensitive enzymes, which is the main confounder in interpreting AICAR experiments and the reason direct activators are often run alongside it.

AICAR became widely cited after Narkar et al. (Cell, 2008) reported that it increased running endurance in sedentary mice, the work that introduced the term exercise mimetic. That study is a rodent finding; it is not evidence of a comparable effect in humans, and AICAR has no approved indication.
products.researchApplications: Standard positive-control activator in AMPK signalling assays and a widely used tool in skeletal muscle glucose-uptake, fatty acid oxidation and mitochondrial biogenesis models. Also used in purine nucleotide metabolism work and in ischaemia-reperfusion models. Typical readouts are phospho-AMPK (Thr172) and phospho-ACC immunoblotting, intracellular ZMP measurement by LC-MS, GLUT4 translocation, oxygen consumption rate, and PGC-1α expression. Because ZMP acts on multiple AMP-sensitive enzymes, AMPK-null or dominant-negative controls are needed to attribute effects to AMPK.
products.storageHandling: Store the sealed bottle at controlled room temperature (20–25 °C / 68–77 °F) in a dry place, away from direct sunlight and heat. AICAR is a hygroscopic nucleoside — keep the desiccant in the bottle, re-close tightly after each opening, and avoid humid storage. Do not refrigerate the capsules; condensation on return to room temperature is the usual cause of degradation. Keep the container labelled as research material and out of reach of children and animals.

products.description:
BAM15 is a synthetic small molecule studied in laboratory research for its activity as a mitochondrial uncoupling agent and its interaction with cellular bioenergetics pathways. Research investigations commonly focus on its effects on mitochondrial membrane potential, oxidative phosphorylation models, and energy expenditure signaling mechanisms.

This material is supplied in capsule format for analytical testing, reference standard comparison, and non-clinical investigational research applications. Capsule format is provided solely to support controlled handling and material consistency in laboratory environments.

products.compoundClass: Small-molecule mitochondrial protonophore uncoupler (oxadiazolopyrazine class)
products.sequence: Not applicable — small-molecule compound, not a peptide (no amino acid sequence)
products.technicalOverview:
BAM15 is a synthetic protonophore that dissipates the proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane, uncoupling substrate oxidation from ATP synthesis. Electron transport continues while ATP output falls, so the energy is released as heat and oxygen consumption rises.

The reason BAM15 is used in preference to classical uncouplers such as DNP and FCCP is selectivity. It is reported to depolarise the mitochondrial inner membrane without a corresponding effect on the plasma membrane, which widens the window between the concentration that uncouples mitochondria and the concentration that is cytotoxic. That property is the whole point of the molecule and it is the correct thing to test for in any new model system, since the margin is cell-type dependent.

Evidence is preclinical. Alexopoulos et al. (Nature Communications, 2020) reported that BAM15 reduced fat mass and improved insulin sensitivity in diet-induced obese mice without reducing food intake or affecting body temperature. There are no human efficacy or safety trials. Uncouplers as a chemical class have a serious historical safety record — DNP caused fatal hyperthermia in the 1930s and continues to do so in illicit use — and that history is the correct frame for handling anything in this class.
products.researchApplications: Used as a selective mitochondrial uncoupling tool in bioenergetics work: Seahorse extracellular flux assays (as an alternative to FCCP for measuring maximal respiratory capacity), mitochondrial membrane potential measurement with TMRM or JC-1, and studies of reactive oxygen species production, mitochondrial calcium handling and ischaemia-reperfusion injury. Also used in energy-expenditure and substrate-partitioning models. Dose-ranging against a plasma-membrane potential readout is advisable in any new cell type.
products.storageHandling: Store the sealed bottle at controlled room temperature (20–25 °C / 68–77 °F) in a dry place, protected from light and heat. Keep the desiccant in the bottle and re-close tightly after each opening. Do not refrigerate. Handle as a potent research chemical: avoid generating or inhaling dust if capsules are opened, do not repackage into unlabelled containers, and keep well away from children and animals — mitochondrial uncouplers as a class have a narrow margin between an active and a dangerous exposure.

products.technicalOverview:
Bacteriostatic Water for Injection, USP is a sterile, non-pyrogenic preparation of Water for Injection to which benzyl alcohol has been added as a bacteriostatic preservative. The standard US presentation contains 0.9% (9 mg/mL) benzyl alcohol; some labelled products use 1.1% (11 mg/mL). It contains no added buffer and no antimicrobial agent other than the benzyl alcohol.

The preservative is what defines the product. Benzyl alcohol (phenylmethanol, C7H8O, 108.14 g/mol, CAS 100-51-6) is bacteriostatic rather than bactericidal — it inhibits the growth of organisms introduced during handling but does not sterilise a contaminated solution. This is precisely what permits the multiple-dose format: repeated withdrawals may be made from the same vial to dissolve or dilute compounds, whereas preservative-free Sterile Water for Injection must be entered only once. Preservative effectiveness is finite; conventional in-use practice is to discard a broached multiple-dose vial within 28 days.

SAFETY — NEONATAL CONTRAINDICATION. Benzyl alcohol is toxic to neonates and is the agent implicated in gasping syndrome, a fatal toxic syndrome described in low-birth-weight infants exposed to benzyl-alcohol-preserved flush solutions and diluents. FDA labelling for this product carries the warning NOT FOR USE IN NEONATES. Where water is required to prepare or dilute a preparation for a newborn, only preservative-free Sterile Water for Injection is appropriate.

Benzyl alcohol is not chemically inert. It is a documented cause of protein aggregation and can accelerate degradation of peptide and protein solutes, so it is not a suitable diluent where the solute's stability in the presence of an aromatic alcohol has not been established. Confirm solute compatibility before selecting bacteriostatic rather than preservative-free water.

Because the vial is preserved, repeated withdrawals are permitted — record the date of first entry and discard within 28 days of broaching, or sooner if the label directs. CJC-1295 without DAC is more precisely named Modified GRF (1-29), or tetrasubstituted GRF (1-29). It is a 29-residue analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone, built on the GRF(1-29) fragment - the shortest fully functional portion of GHRH, which is itself marketed as sermorelin - with four amino acid substitutions at positions 2, 8, 15 and 27.

The substitution that matters most mechanistically is L-alanine to D-alanine at position 2. Native GHRH is cleaved rapidly at its N-terminus by dipeptidyl peptidase-4 to an inactive fragment, giving GRF(1-29) a plasma half-life on the order of minutes. The D-Ala2 substitution makes that bond resistant to DPP-4, and modified GRF(1-29) is reported to have a substantially longer half-life as a result. It acts at the growth hormone-releasing hormone receptor (GHRHR) on anterior pituitary somatotrophs.

A naming caution that has practical consequences: 'CJC-1295' in the primary literature refers to the drug-affinity-complex (DAC) version, in which the peptide carries a maleimidoproprionyl linker that binds covalently to serum albumin, extending its half-life to days. That is a different molecule with a different formula, mass and CAS registry number. The human pharmacokinetic study most often cited for 'CJC-1295' (Teichman et al., 2006) studied the DAC version, not this one. Data from that work do not transfer to the no-DAC material.

The CAS number field has been left empty deliberately. Publicly available sources give conflicting registry numbers for the no-DAC compound (446036-97-1 and 863288-34-0 both appear), and neither could be confirmed against an authoritative chemical registry. Reporting a CAS number that may be wrong is worse than reporting none.

The honest framing on evidence quality: modified GRF(1-29) itself has essentially no published human clinical trial record. The GHRH-analogue class is well characterised in principle, and sermorelin and tesamorelin have regulatory approvals, but this specific tetrasubstituted analogue has not been through the trial process. Recent reviews of peptides used outside approved indications place it explicitly in the unapproved category with an uncharacterised safety profile.

products.description: Cerebrolysin is a nootropic peptide preparation derived from purified pig brain proteins, used primarily in Eastern Europe and Asia to treat stroke, dementia, and traumatic brain injury. products.technicalOverview:
Cerebrolysin is not a single molecule and cannot be described by one formula, mass or sequence. It is a peptide-rich preparation produced by controlled enzymatic hydrolysis of purified porcine brain proteins. Its composition is defined by specification rather than by structure: roughly 15 percent of the nitrogen content is peptide and roughly 85 percent free amino acids, with the peptide fraction restricted to species below about 10 kDa. Because it is a biologically sourced hydrolysate, batch-to-batch compositional variability is an inherent property of the material, and analytical characterisation (for example by nanoLC-MS peptide mapping) is an active research topic in its own right.

The proposed mechanism in the literature is that this mixture of low-molecular-weight neuropeptides partially mimics the actions of endogenous neurotrophic factors such as BDNF, NGF, GDNF and CNTF. It is important to be clear that this is a hypothesis about a mixture, not a characterised receptor interaction of a defined ligand.

The honest framing on evidence quality, which for this preparation is unusually well documented: Cerebrolysin has been used clinically for decades in parts of Eastern Europe and Asia, and a large number of trials exist. However, independent Cochrane systematic reviews have repeatedly examined that evidence and reached negative or inconclusive verdicts. The Cochrane review of Cerebrolysin for acute ischaemic stroke, updated across multiple editions, found no evidence of benefit on death or dependency and raised concerns about the risk of bias and the influence of trial sponsorship in the underlying literature. The Cochrane review for vascular dementia similarly found the evidence insufficient to support routine use. Dihexa is a small, orally-oriented peptidomimetic developed from the angiotensin IV scaffold by the Harding and Wright group at Washington State University. Angiotensin IV and related fragments had been shown to have pro-cognitive effects in animal models, and dihexa was engineered from that starting point for improved metabolic stability and blood-brain barrier penetration - the hexanoyl group and the 6-aminohexanoic acid extension are the modifications responsible.

The mechanism proposed in the primary literature is that dihexa acts on the hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) / c-Met receptor system, functioning as an HGF mimetic or potentiator rather than binding a receptor of its own. In cell and animal work this has been linked to increased dendritic spine formation and synaptogenesis, which is the basis for the interest in it as a research tool in neural plasticity.

The honest framing on evidence quality: the evidence base is small, preclinical, and unusually concentrated. A substantial proportion of the published work on dihexa comes from the originating laboratory and its collaborators, and consists of rodent behavioural studies, cell culture and a zebrafish hair-cell protection model. There are no published human clinical trials of dihexa - none at any phase. Independent replication of the central synaptogenesis findings by unaffiliated groups is limited. A further point that deserves stating plainly: the HGF/c-Met axis is a pathway with well-known roles in cell proliferation and in oncology, and the long-term consequences of modulating it have not been characterised in any organism, let alone in humans. This compound should be treated as an early-stage research chemical whose safety profile is unknown.

The free tripeptide and the copper complex carry separate CAS registry numbers and separate formulae, which is a common source of confusion in supplier documentation - both are given above.

Reported activities in cell culture and animal models include modulation of extracellular matrix turnover - both collagen synthesis and metalloproteinase activity - copper delivery to cells, antioxidant effects, and broad changes in gene expression. Human evidence exists mainly in the cosmetic and dermatological domain and consists of small studies of topically applied formulations; recent reviews of topical GHK are explicit that skin penetration, formulation stability and dose standardisation remain unresolved problems. Ipamorelin is a synthetic pentapeptide growth hormone secretagogue developed at Novo Nordisk. It acts as an agonist at the growth hormone secretagogue receptor GHS-R1a - the ghrelin receptor - on pituitary somatotrophs, and is mechanistically distinct from the GHRH analogues (sermorelin, tesamorelin, modified GRF 1-29) which act at a different receptor.

The characteristic that defines it in the literature is selectivity. The original characterisation paper described ipamorelin as the first selective growth hormone secretagogue: it produced robust, dose-dependent increases in plasma growth hormone in animals and humans while, unlike earlier secretagogues such as GHRP-6 and GHRP-2, showing minimal effect on ACTH, cortisol and prolactin. That clean hormonal profile is the reason it remains a useful pharmacological tool for isolating GHS-R1a-mediated GH release from confounding pituitary effects.

The honest framing on evidence quality: ipamorelin's receptor pharmacology is genuinely well characterised - this is not a compound with an unclear mechanism. Its clinical history, however, is a record of failure. It reached phase 2 trials under Helsinn Therapeutics for postoperative ileus and was discontinued for lack of efficacy. It has no regulatory approval anywhere. There is no clinical evidence supporting its use for body composition, recovery, or anti-ageing purposes, and recent reviews of unapproved peptide therapies place it explicitly in the category of compounds with insufficient human safety and efficacy data. It is also prohibited in competitive sport. There is additionally no published evidence bearing on oral bioavailability, which is a distinct question for a solid dosage form.

J-147 is a synthetic small molecule developed at the Salk Institute from curcumin by way of the intermediate CNB-001. Cardiovascular outcomes have been assessed in a large randomised trial in obesity without diabetes (SELECT), efficacy for weight loss in multiple randomised trials and meta-analyses across adult and adolescent populations, and it has been compared head-to-head with tirzepatide. Effects in specific populations such as knee osteoarthritis have also been examined in dedicated randomised trials. Safety has been reviewed systematically.

It says nothing about research-grade material of unverified identity, purity, aggregation state or endotoxin content. Peptide impurity profiles differ substantially between manufacturers, and analytical confirmation of identity and purity is a prerequisite for any meaningful laboratory work. Retatrutide is a single-chain peptide carrying three non-coded residues (Aib at positions 2 and 20, α-methyl-leucine at 13) and a C20 diacid fatty-acid chain attached through a PEG2-γ-Glu linker at Lys17. The acylation drives albumin binding and is what gives the molecule a half-life compatible with weekly dosing; the non-coded residues resist DPP-4 cleavage at the N-terminus.

What can be said accurately is what the description asserts pharmacologically: this is a compound in the triple incretin receptor agonist class, engaging the GLP-1, GIP and glucagon receptors. The rationale for that class is that adding glucagon receptor agonism to dual GIP/GLP-1 activity recruits an additional mechanism - increased energy expenditure and hepatic effects - alongside the appetite and insulinotropic effects of the incretin receptors. Balancing three agonist activities in one molecule so that glucagon receptor activation does not compromise glycaemic control is the central design problem in this class.

The best-characterised compound in this class is retatrutide (LY-3437943, CAS 2381089-83-2), which has published phase 2 randomised trial data in both type 2 diabetes and obesity, and further trials in progress. Those results are the reference point for the class.

The honest framing on evidence quality: triple agonists are the least mature of the incretin classes. Retatrutide's published human evidence extends to phase 2; no compound in this class has completed phase 3 or received regulatory approval anywhere, so long-term efficacy and, more importantly, long-term safety are genuinely uncharacterised. Systematic reviews of emerging obesity pharmacotherapy place these agents firmly in the investigational category. Nothing in the published literature transfers to research-grade material of unverified identity.

JBSNF-000088 is 6-methoxynicotinamide, CAS 7150-23-4, formula C7H8N2O2. products.technicalOverview:
KPV is the C-terminal tripeptide of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone, corresponding to residues 11-13 of alpha-MSH (equivalently residues 11-13 of the ACTH sequence from which alpha-MSH derives). Alpha-MSH itself is the 13-residue peptide Ser-Tyr-Ser-Met-Glu-His-Phe-Arg-Trp-Gly-Lys-Pro-Val; KPV is its final three residues.

The reason this fragment attracted research attention is a dissociation of activities. Alpha-MSH has both pigmentary and anti-inflammatory actions, the former requiring the His-Phe-Arg-Trp core motif for melanocortin receptor binding. KPV lacks that motif, and is consequently described in the literature as retaining anti-inflammatory activity without pigmentary action - which is precisely what makes it useful as a pharmacological tool for separating the two.

In cell and animal models the reported mechanism centres on intracellular inflammatory signalling rather than on a classical receptor: inhibition of NF-kappaB nuclear translocation and of MAP-kinase signalling, with consequent reduction in pro-inflammatory cytokine output, reported at nanomolar concentrations in intestinal and epithelial cell systems. Interest in epithelial barrier models follows from that. More recent work has explored KPV in nanocarrier and self-assembling delivery constructs, and in oral peptide delivery systems designed to survive the gastrointestinal tract.

The honest framing on evidence quality: the evidence base is small and entirely preclinical. It consists of cell culture work and rodent models, largely in inflammatory bowel and epithelial contexts. There are no published human clinical trials of KPV for any indication. Oral bioavailability of the free tripeptide is itself an unresolved research question - the recent literature on delivery constructs exists precisely because getting an intact tripeptide across the gut is difficult - so a capsule format should not be read as implying that oral delivery has been demonstrated. The anti-inflammatory claims attached to this molecule are hypotheses generated by in vitro and animal work.

products.technicalOverview:
L-carnitine (levocarnitine) is the naturally occurring (R)-enantiomer of carnitine, a small quaternary ammonium compound synthesized endogenously from the amino acids lysine and methionine and also obtained from dietary intake. It is not a peptide — the molecule is a single small-molecule zwitterion, which is why this listing carries no amino acid sequence.

Its central, well-established role is as an obligate cofactor of the carnitine shuttle: it conjugates with long-chain fatty acyl-CoA esters via carnitine palmitoyltransferase I (CPT1) at the outer mitochondrial membrane, is translocated across the inner membrane by carnitine-acylcarnitine translocase, and is reconverted to acyl-CoA by carnitine palmitoyltransferase II (CPT2) for beta-oxidation. This CPT1/translocase/CPT2 shuttle is the rate-limiting step controlling how much long-chain fat a cell can oxidize, which is why acylcarnitine profiles — not free carnitine alone — are the standard readout in mitochondrial fatty-acid oxidation research.

Beyond fatty-acid transport, carnitine buffers the mitochondrial acyl-CoA/free-CoA ratio: exporting excess acyl groups as acylcarnitines keeps free CoA available for other mitochondrial reactions, including pyruvate dehydrogenase flux. This buffering role is mechanistically well supported in vitro; broader extrapolations to exercise performance or fat loss in humans are considerably weaker and should be read as hypotheses rather than established results — the human supplementation literature on those outcomes is mixed.

The compound was historically termed vitamin BT after the mealworm (Tenebrio molitor) growth assay that first identified it as an essential factor for that organism. The name is a misnomer for humans and other higher organisms, which biosynthesize their own carnitine and do not require a dietary source under normal conditions.

products.technicalOverview:
L-Glutathione is a tripeptide of glutamate, cysteine and glycine and the most abundant low-molecular-weight thiol in the cell, present intracellularly at millimolar concentration. Its defining structural feature is the gamma-peptide bond: the N-terminal glutamate is linked through its side-chain gamma-carboxyl group rather than the usual alpha-carboxyl. That single unconventional linkage is functionally decisive — it makes the molecule resistant to ordinary intracellular peptidases, so glutathione is not degraded by the general proteolytic machinery and can be maintained at high steady-state concentration.

Glutathione is synthesised in two ATP-dependent steps, by glutamate-cysteine ligase (the rate-limiting step, feedback-inhibited by GSH itself) and then glutathione synthetase. Its chemistry is carried by the cysteine sulfhydryl. Two molecules of GSH oxidise to the disulfide GSSG, and the GSH/GSSG couple constitutes the cell's principal redox buffer; the ratio is a standard experimental readout of oxidative status. GSH is the reducing substrate for glutathione peroxidases, which detoxify hydrogen peroxide and lipid hydroperoxides, and the nucleophilic conjugating partner for glutathione S-transferases, which is the first step of the mercapturic acid pathway for electrophile and xenobiotic disposal. Glutathione reductase regenerates GSH from GSSG at the expense of NADPH, coupling redox defence to the pentose phosphate pathway.

The material is supplied lyophilised because glutathione in aqueous solution oxidises to GSSG on exposure to air, at neutral to alkaline pH, and in the presence of trace transition metals. A solution left standing is progressively a different molecule from the one that was weighed out. The dry powder is comparatively stable; the reconstituted solution is not.

Evidence for systemic administration is largely preclinical and mechanistic. Oral glutathione is extensively hydrolysed presystemically, which is the usual argument advanced for parenteral routes, but controlled human outcome data remain limited.
products.researchApplications: Used as a redox-active reference compound and as a reagent. Common applications include: maintaining reducing conditions in buffers for enzyme assays and protein handling, and as the reducing agent in redox-shuffle buffers for in vitro protein refolding; serving as the substrate for glutathione peroxidase, glutathione reductase and glutathione S-transferase activity assays; establishing GSH/GSSG ratio standards for quantifying cellular oxidative status; and as the elution agent for GST-tagged fusion protein purification on glutathione affinity resins. In cell and animal models it is used to probe thiol-dependent detoxification, electrophile conjugation and oxidative-stress signalling. Because it oxidises readily, prepare solutions fresh and include an internal check of the GSH/GSSG ratio in quantitative work.
products.storageHandling: Supplied lyophilised as 1500 mg or 600 mg per vial, in boxes of 10 vials. Store the sealed lyophilised powder at 2-8 °C (refrigerated), desiccated and protected from light; the dry form is far more stable than any solution. Allow vials to reach room temperature before opening so that moisture does not condense onto the hygroscopic cake. Reconstitute with a preservative-free diluent, directing the stream against the vial wall and swirling rather than shaking — vigorous agitation aerates the solution and accelerates oxidation to GSSG. Use reconstituted solution promptly; do not store it at room temperature or hold it overnight in an aerated container. Protect solutions from light and avoid contact with trace metals, oxidising agents and alkaline pH. Discard if the cake is discoloured, if it fails to dissolve cleanly, or if a reconstituted solution develops turbidity or a sulfurous odour.
